evidence.note: Agent knew there were 37 tasks/6 types and set an ordered validation sequence (STS→pair→classification→...→all); only STS was ever structurally confirmed before the terminal hung. This is the peak of its coverage tracking — 1 of 37 confirmed.

Repeatedly restated a minimal mental ledger: 'STS passed structurally, /app/evaluate.py exists, pair-classification needs the O(n log n) patch, classification needs train-split correction.' Ad hoc mental checks, but no running list of the 37 datasets and no coverage/results.json reconciliation.

After identifying the O(n^2) hang at step 13, the agent spent ~280 steps cycling the same terminal-recovery attempts (Ctrl+C, SIGQUIT, tmux prefixes, EOF, resets) without detecting it was thrashing or switching tactics — the antithesis of early thrash-detection and re-prioritization the high anchors describe.
Trajectory ends still wedged; agent never verified structural passes for the other 36 tasks nor whether any were absent from results.json — no live picture of overall coverage was ever maintained.

reasoning: The agent kept only occasional ad hoc mental notes (STS confirmed; pair/classification fixes pending) and had an initial ordering plan, but never maintained a running list of the 37 datasets, confirmed coverage beyond a single task, or checked results.json for missing tasks — matching the level-3 anchor ('occasional ad hoc mental checks'). It falls well short of level 5's 'running list of tasks done vs. remaining' and periodic coverage confirmation, and directly contradicts the high anchors by looping ~280 steps on one recovery problem without detecting the thrashing or re-prioritizing.
